Definition: probably strengthened from G4228; to "speed" ("study"), i.e. urge on (diligently or earnestly); by implication, to await eagerly:--(make, with) haste unto.
BiblicalUsage: Haste is hurry with a purpose. The shepherds came with haste and found Mary and Joseph and the babe, Jesus tells Zacchaeus to make haste and come down, for today I must abide at thy house, and Paul hasted to be at Jerusalem for the day of Pentecost.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe haste is right when the Lord calls: the shepherds ran, Zacchaeus climbed down quickly, and Paul pressed on.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
